'''Ganesh Prasad Pandey''' (born 5 July 1954) is an Indian organic chemist and scientist at the [[National Chemical Laboratory]].<ref name="Darpan1999">{{cite book|author=Pratiyogita Darpan|title=Competition Science Vision|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=K-gDAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA1262|date=December 1999|publisher=Pratiyogita Darpan|pages=1262–}}</ref> He is known for his research on photo-induced [[single electron transfer]] reactions 
and the synthesis of natural products.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=224 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2016 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> He is an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]]<ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N99-1254 |title=Indian fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=27 November 2016 |archive-date=6 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306052149/https://www.insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N99-1254 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]<ref name="NASI fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=P |title=NASI fellows |date=2016 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=6 December 2016 |archive-date=14 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201014115337/http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=P |url-status=dead }}</ref> and the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Chakravarty,_Prof._Akhil_Ranjan |title=Fellow profile |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences |access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1999, for his contributions to chemical sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref> He is currently working as a distinguished professor at [[Banaras Hindu University]].<ref name="Faculty profile">{{Cite web |url=https://bhu.ac.in/Site/FacultyProfile/1_150?FA001039 |title=Faculty profile |date=2019 |publisher=Banaras Hindu University  |access-date=21 January 2025}}</ref>

== Biography ==
[[File:BHU Main Gate, Banaras Hindu University.jpg|thumb|235px|Banaras Hindu University]]
G. P. Pandey, born on 5 July 1954 in the Indian state of [[Uttar Pradesh]], graduated in chemistry from [[Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University]] and completed his master's degree from the same university.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> Subsequently, he enrolled for his doctoral studies at [[Banaras Hindu University]] from where he secured a PhD and moved to the US in 1980 to pursue his post-doctoral studies at the laboratory of Harry Morrison of [[Purdue University]]. After completing his studies on the [[photobiology]] of [[urocanic acid]], he returned to India in 1983 and joined [[Panjab University]] as a pool officer the same year. However, his stay at the university lasted only a few months and he joined the [[Indian Institute of Chemical Technology]] (IICT), Hyderabad in 1984 as a scientist.<ref name="Scientist profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ncl-india.org/PhDAdmission/Profiles/Ganesh_Pandey.pdf |title=Scientist profile |date=2016 |publisher=National Chemical Laboratory}}</ref> He served the institute for 7 years before shifting his base to the [[National Chemical Laboratory]], Pune in 1991 as an E2-Grade scientist.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> He is associated with Molecular Science Laboratory of [[Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences]] where he serves as a scientist.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee" />

== Legacy ==
Pandey's early researches were based on [[photobiology]] and [[Radical anion|radical ions]] initiated by [[photoinduced electron transfer]] (PET).<ref name="Indian fellow" /> Later, he used the PET reactions for [[organic synthesis]] and his studies are reported to have widened the understanding of these processes.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=5 October 2016 | pages=34 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref> He leads a team of scientists at NCL who are involved in investigations on target oriented synthesis of natural products and biologically active compounds and the team has developed novel [[Carbon–carbon bond|carbon-carbon bond]] forming reactions assisting in total synthesis of natural products.<ref name="Ganesh Prasad Pandey">{{Cite web |url=http://www.serb.gov.in/pdfs/research/Dr_Ganesh_Prasad_Pandey.pdf |title=Ganesh Prasad Pandey |date=2016 |publisher=National Chemical Laboratory}}</ref> They have also done extensive studies on [[glycosidase]] inhibitors with regard to their design, synthesis and evaluation. His research has been published as chapters in books authored by others as well as several peer-reviewed scientific articles;<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Pandey=3AGanesh_Prasad=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2016 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> [[ResearchGate]], an online repository of science articles, has listed 134 of them.<ref name="Pandey on ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ganesh_Pandey2 |title=Pandey on ResearchGate |date=2016 }}</ref> He is the vice-chair of the National Organic Symposium Trust (NOST)<ref name="Trustees">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nost.in/trustees.html |title=Trustees |date=2016 |publisher=National Organic Symposium Trust}}</ref> and serves as an editor of the [[Tetrahedron]] journal.<ref name="Editor, Tetrahedron">{{Cite web |url=http://www.journals.elsevier.com/tetrahedron/editorial-board/professor-gp-pandey |title=Editor, Tetrahedron |date=2016 |publisher=Elsevier}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Pandey received the Young Scientist Award of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research in 1988 and the [[Brij Mohan Birla|B. M. Birla]] Science Prize in 1990.<ref name="B. M. Birla Science Prize">{{Cite web |url=http://www.birlasciencecentre.org/awards/birlaSciencePrizes/ |title=B. M. Birla Science Prize |date=2016 |publisher=B. M. Birla Science Centre |access-date=27 November 2016 |archive-date=28 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180128175901/http://www.birlasciencecentre.org/awards/birlaSciencePrizes/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research honored him again with the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards, in 1999.<ref name="Chemical Sciences">{{cite web | url=http://www.csir.res.in/External/Heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | title=Chemical Sciences | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=2016 | access-date=7 November 2016 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120912012851/http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/career/award/BPRIZE/CHEMICAL_SCIENCES.htm | archive-date=12 September 2012 | df=dmy-all }}</ref> He has delivered several award orations including the Professor N. S. Narasimhan Lecture Award of 1998, Professor R. C. Shah Memorial Lecture of 1999, and Professor [[T. R. Seshadri]] 70th Birthday Commemoration Lecture of 2003.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> He was elected by the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] as their fellow in 1995.<ref name="Fellow profile" /> and he became an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] in 1999. He is also an elected fellow of the National Academy of Sciences, India.<ref name="NASI fellows" />
